name: kinu
description: Kinu gives AI agents a durable computer of their own. It adapts and improves with use, runs locally or fully in the cloud, and solves hard tasks by exploring multiple approaches and letting executable checks choose the winner.

scripts.test: bun test --parallel=4 packages/agent-core/ packages/agent-utils/ packages/core/ packages/compaction/
scripts.test:workerd: vitest run --root packages/cf-backend tests/workerd/ && vitest run --root packages/devbox tests/workerd/
scripts.check: bun run lint && bun test packages/agent-core/drift.test.ts && tsc --noEmit -p packages/agent-utils && tsc --noEmit -p packages/core && tsc --noEmit -p packages/compaction && tsc --noEmit -p packages/cf-backend && tsc --noEmit -p packages/cf-backend/tests/workerd && tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli-backend && tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli && tsc --noEmit -p packages/devbox && tsc --noEmit -p packages/devbox/tests/workerd && tsc --noEmit -p packages/test-utils && tsc --noEmit -p tests && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/tsconfig.scripts.json && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/fixtures/r2-bench && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/fixtures/kinu-durability && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/fixtures/hardening-runtime && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/fixtures/payload-transport && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/fixtures/fuse-probe && node --check packages/pc-agent/src/index.js && node --check packages/pc-agent/src/sandbox.js && node --check packages/pc-agent/src/pty.js && bun run gate:typecheck-coverage
scripts.test:anti-slop: tsc --noEmit -p tools/oxlint/anti-slop && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/rules.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/drift.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-swallow.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-wait-until.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-ambient-git.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-copy-rpc-stub.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-untyped-console.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/import-extension.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/typescript-escapes.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-elapsed-deadline.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/type-aware.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/no-vacuous-type-predicate.gate.test.ts && node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types tools/oxlint/anti-slop/live-tree.gate.test.ts

//dependencies:@ai-sdk: The AI SDK v6 packages are pinned EXACTLY, here and in every workspace that declares one, because upstream pins them to each other exactly: `ai@6.0.214` requires `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.33` and `@ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.139` by exact version, and each provider does the same. A caret on any one of them therefore does not age it independently — it floats that package ahead of the rest and bun answers with a SECOND copy of the SDK nested under whichever parent disagreed, which is how `@ai-sdk/provider` came to be installed twice while both manifests named one version. So the cohort moves as one edit. This one is GHSA-866g-f22w-33x8 (CVE-2026-8769, uncontrolled resource consumption in provider-utils' response handlers), whose first patched release on the v6 line is provider-utils 4.0.33; these are the earliest same-major releases that pin it. Later v6 releases exist and are also patched, but from `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@2.0.70` the provider throws its own "Response stream ended without a finish reason" before a finish-step lands, which pre-empts the dead-stream detector in packages/core/src/chat.ts and the two contracts unit-chat-stream-integrity.test.ts holds over it. Moving past that boundary is a stream-integrity decision, not a dependency refresh.
//overrides: @cloudflare/containers is pinned here because @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.8 declares `^0.3.5`, and the lock resolved that range to a SECOND copy at 0.3.6 nested under the SDK. That nested copy was the only one the deployed Worker ever bound: the top-level 0.3.7 both workspaces pin contributed zero runtime bytes, because the one import of it in the tree is a type import. So the pinned and documented version was not the version that ran, and 0.3.7's container state-machine fix — setStoppedIfUnchanged, `setRunning` moved later in the start path, and the pre-onStop state threaded through callOnStop so a stop cannot overwrite a newer state — never shipped. 0.3.7 satisfies the SDK's own range, so this reconciles the two resolutions rather than forcing an incompatible one. Removing the entry is only safe once the SDK's own range no longer resolves to anything else; scripts/nested-container-resolution.test.ts holds the manifests, the lockfile, the installed graph and the emitted artifact to one version, so a reintroduced copy is red.
//overrides:@ai-sdk/react: @ai-sdk/react is pinned here, not in a workspace manifest, because it reaches this tree ONLY as an auto-installed peer — `agents`, `@cloudflare/ai-chat` and `@cloudflare/think` all declare it and no manifest of ours does, so no dependency range of ours can move it. It is the react member of the exactly-pinned AI SDK v6 cohort above (`3.0.216` requires `ai@6.0.214`), and it is pinned for the same reason plus one of its own. The cohort reason: left behind, it does not merely age — its `ai` and `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` dependencies are exact pins, so it nests a complete second AI SDK beneath itself. That is how GHSA-866g-f22w-33x8 survived the first attempt at this fix: every declared range moved to the patched cohort and `@ai-sdk/react@3.0.198` kept the vulnerable `@ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.27` alive at `@ai-sdk/react/@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, one level down where no manifest bump reaches. Its own reason: the peer ranges those three packages declare are `^3.0.0 || ^4.0.0`, and 4.x pins `ai@7`, so any range here that admits 4.x lets a resolution move this repository off AI SDK v6 without anyone asking. Note that bun does NOT retroactively apply an override to a peer already resolved in the lockfile — it warns `incorrect peer dependency` and keeps the old one — so changing this entry needs the stale `@ai-sdk/react` lockfile entries dropped before the resolve, not just an edit here. Removing the entry is safe once some workspace manifest declares @ai-sdk/react directly.
//overrides:sharp: sharp is pinned here because every published miniflare pins `sharp: 0.35.2` EXACTLY — all sixteen 5.x releases, up to and including 5.20260908.0-alpha, the one wrangler 4.130.0 depends on — and 0.35.2 is what GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c names: two libheif heap overflows (GHSA-g89c-p67h-r497 / CVE-2026-84383 and GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545), high, fixed in 0.35.4. So no wrangler or miniflare range of ours can move it and an override is the only lever. It is NOT an optional dependency: miniflare declares `sharp` under `dependencies`, and what is optional is sharp's own per-platform binary — on this box `@img/sharp-linux-x64` and `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64` are both installed and the libvips shared object carries the libheif symbols, so this override moves real installed bytes rather than only the lockfile. 0.35.4 is a patch release inside the minor the exact pin already named. Reached only through dev tooling (wrangler and @cloudflare/vite-plugin, and the vitest workers pool under them), so nothing the Worker serves decodes an image with it.
//overrides:hono: hono is pinned here because the resolve landed TWO copies below 4.13.5 and neither is reachable by a range of ours: 4.13.2 under `@cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.8` (which declares `^4.13.0`, and which `@hono/node-server`'s `^4` peer also lands on) and 4.12.23 under `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0` (which declares `^4.11.4`). Both are hit by GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv, GHSA-g6gw-c38x-mqfc and GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx — a `toSSG()` write outside the output directory, unbounded dot-notation nesting in `parseBody()`, and a query parser that reads past the URL fragment — all three fixed in 4.13.5. 4.13.7 is the current publish and satisfies both declared ranges and the peer, so this reconciles the two resolutions onto the patched line rather than forcing an incompatible one, and it collapses them to one copy. Note what it also does: the twelve advisories the `hono` REVIEWED_ADVISORIES entry used to accept were all against the 4.12.23 copy, and moving it past them is why that entry is gone rather than edited.
